A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and the removal of one redundant plot.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on synthetic key-value, news-article, and LLM-agent datasets in Tables I–IV, with additional hyperparameter analyses in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains these original evaluations in Tables 1–4 and the hyperparameter analyses in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the prompt-based and kNN-LM implementations, output regeneration, and Appendix A's Shapley pruning heuristic are unchanged. Efficiency optimizations move to Section 6.3; alternative influence estimators are discussed prospectively rather than introduced into the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic key-value, news-article, and LLM-agent datasets, including the same retrieval scenarios and web, email, and calendar tool tasks. The new threat-model discussion adds no evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: The synthetic comparison retains the same prompt-based, kNN-LM, and introspection rows, while the agent comparison retains prompt-based propagation and introspection. Newly cited security systems are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: The reported models, dataset sizes, metrics, retrieval procedures, and thresholds remain unchanged. Examples include 14-document synthetic contexts, the 63-question introspection evaluation, Llama-2 7B/70B configurations, and the agent experiment's lambda = 0.2.

E4.justification: Both versions retain model-size comparisons, perplexity-tolerance sweeps, Shapley-pruning analyses, retrieval comparisons, and output-regeneration alignment analyses. V1's removed Figure 7 displays model-size results still present in v2's Table 1 and Section 5.1.

E5.justification: Table I/1 retains the same mean and one-standard-deviation reporting for macro-averaged precision and recall. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables I–IV match Tables 1–4 numerically, and Appendix A's heatmap values are identical. For example, synthetic prompt-based exact match remains 85.94% at both model sizes, and agent label improvement remains 85.0% and 95.0%. The removed model-size plot contains no unique results.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 newly states explicit security assumptions: input labels are correct, and adversary capabilities and illicit-flow goals are specified. The lattice definitions, lambda-similarity definition, Equations 1–4, Proposition 1, and its correctness argument remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain, but the abstract changes 'improves the label' in more than 85% of agent cases to 'improves over the baseline,' following its identification of introspection as the baseline. This changes the implied comparison: unchanged Table 3 reports label-improvement rates of 85%/95% versus introspection's 45%/80%, not an over-85% head-to-head win rate.

C2.justification: V2 adds practical label-provenance examples and explicit threat boundaries in Section 2.1. Section 6.3 newly discusses attention sinks and lost-in-the-middle effects as obstacles to attention-based influence estimation. Existing monotonicity, computational-cost, and adversarial degradation limitations remain.

D1.justification: The new Open Science section promises to release the prototype implementation and evaluation datasets. This adds release information, but supplies no access link or evidence of an actual release. Existing implementation settings and optimization guidance are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds comparisons with Wu et al.'s information-flow defense and Balunovic et al.'s security monitor, and explicitly connects the method to secure multi-execution. It condenses the broader influence-estimation survey, removes several training-data valuation citations, and adds attention-sinks and lost-in-the-middle references.

P1.justification: V2 tightens prose, standardizes 'prompt-based' terminology, moves optimization discussion into Extensions, and shortens the conclusion and influence-estimation survey. Open Science and Ethics sections replace the acknowledgements section. Most technical exposition and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 changes typography, heading styles, the author block, and display placement. It removes the redundant model-size plot, expands Figures 4–5's captions, and renumbers retained plots. The remaining figure designs, table structures, and two-column organization are substantially preserved.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves assessability by clarifying label provenance, threat assumptions, and its relationship to existing security systems, while retaining all empirical evidence. These gains are partly offset by the abstract's less precise baseline-comparison claim, which Table 3 does not establish. The Open Science statement is a future commitment, not demonstrated resource availability.
